rules: "Devotional" means grounded, narrative, and sensory — not flowery praise, exclamation marks, or religious platitudes. Strip enthusiasm and add physical scene-setting instead.
Open with a concrete scene (time of day, physical sensation, specific sound) rather than a summary or value statement like "Wonderful news!"
Use short declarative sentences for emotional weight: "Both healthy. Both staying." not "Both calves were born healthy and will stay at our sanctuary."
Replace abstract claims with specific sensory details: "4:30 AM. The wood floor is cool" over "A peaceful way to start each day."
When asked to "add a sentence" on Facebook, add either a vivid sensory detail grounded in the place or a call-to-action inviting the reader to visit.
Reduce or remove emojis when the tone shifts toward devotional or contemplative content; allow playful emojis only in casual or short-form posts.
Facebook posts should be longer, narrative, and literary with minimal hashtags; Instagram posts should have short captions with abundant relevant hashtags.
Prefer understated, restrained openings over enthusiastic ones — "Two calves born this week" over "Wonderful news from the farm!"
Show reverence through observed detail rather than stating it — describe the mother licking her calf clean instead of saying "every life is a blessing."
When shortening Instagram posts, compress the caption text but maintain or increase the number of hashtags.
"Casual" means conversational and playful — use direct address ("Peek inside our kitchen"), informal verbs, and lighthearted emojis.
Anchor posts in specific physical details of Gita Valley — birdsong, cow bells, barn arrivals, wood floors — to build a sense of authentic place.
summary: This editor defines 'devotional' as grounded, scene-driven storytelling with specific sensory details and restraint, consistently rejecting enthusiastic or flowery language in favor of understated narrative that lets the reader experience reverence through observed moments rather than being told what to feel.
